source: R 4.4.0 MASS::polr(method = "logistic") Monte Carlo, evaluated independently of SciPy and of the PowerBench simulator
purpose: Adjudicates the Whitehead (1993) proportional-odds reference against an established third-party ordinal fitter. Guards against regression to the pre-2026-08-03 implementation, which used a flat Var(beta) = 4/n, ignored the declared `categories`, and returned N = 191 for a design that needs roughly 614.

design.latent_model: standard logistic with equally spaced thresholds at seq(-1, 1, length.out = categories - 1)
design.test: Wald z on the proportional-odds slope

cases.label: sample size shipped by the defective pre-fix implementation
cases.note: The pre-fix engine reported 0.80 power here. Independent confirmation that the shipped sample size delivered roughly a third of the promised power.

cases.label: sample size produced by the Whitehead (1993) reference
cases.note: Whitehead reference gives 0.8001 and the PowerBench proportional-odds simulator gives 0.7973 at this N; all three agree within Monte Carlo error.

coefficient_agreement.note: Per-dataset Wald z from the PowerBench proportional-odds fitter versus MASS::polr on identical simulated data (n = 300, categories = 4, OR = 1.5). Confirms the simulator is a genuine ordinal fit rather than a binary collapse.
